3	# Self-Audit Gate
4	
5	> **Scope:** This is the Layer-3 scoring instrument read on demand by the validator-fix-repeat loop
6	> already resident in `SKILL.md`. It scores a completed first-principles analysis against the
7	> six-section output format defined in `references/output-template.md`. The loop instruction
8	> itself — when to apply, what to fix, when to stop — lives in `SKILL.md` under
9	> "Before presenting conclusions" and is **not** repeated here. Come here only to score
10	> an analysis in progress; use `SKILL.md` for the loop procedure and `output-template.md`
11	> for authoring guidance.
12	>
13	> **What this instrument scores:** the structure of *this analysis*. It is not a rubric for the
14	> subject matter. When a request asks for a rubric, scorecard, or grading scheme applied to the
15	> thing being analyzed — an article's argument, a proposal, a design — that is a **separate
16	> deliverable** that belongs in the analysis body. Producing it does not satisfy this gate, and
17	> this gate does not substitute for it. Both must appear. (Historically named the "Validation
18	> Rubric"; renamed because that name collided with subject-matter rubrics and the collision was
19	> observed to cause this gate to be skipped.)

21	## How to Apply This Gate
22	
23	Score the completed analysis against all 6 criteria below. For each criterion, produce exactly
24	one verdict block in the format prescribed in the Verdict Block Format section. An analysis
25	clears this gate only when it satisfies **both** of the following conditions — clearing
26	one condition alone does not constitute a pass:
27	
28	1. **Gate cleared** — no criterion scores Absent.
29	2. **Hand-wavy cap cleared** — at most one criterion scores Hand-wavy.
30	
31	If either condition is not met, revise the analysis and re-score — bounded to **at most one re-perception pass** per analysis, per the rule stated in full under `SKILL.md`'s Turn discipline section. After that single pass, any criterion still failing — or newly failing as a result of the revision — is presented as an unresolved gap with a stated confidence caveat instead of being re-scored again.

33	**Assumption Audit (verify before scoring)**

35	The scan itself is not performed here — the agent already performed it at the end of Phase 4
36	(`SKILL.md`, "End-of-phase Assumption Audit") before this gate is ever applied. This
37	gate's job is narrower: verify the audit ran and its table is exhaustive, not repeat the
38	scan.

40	Before scoring any criterion, confirm the audit table below is present in the analysis and
41	covers every named derivation chain step from section 4 — one row per chain per step, in
42	order, with no step skipped. Do not proceed to verdict blocks until this is confirmed. `Form conforming?` reads `unreached` where a rule binds at a position the mechanical check cannot reach — a disclosed gap in the check, never a softer `no`, and never to be scored as a conforming block. A row whose `Rule applied` cell explains that the check could not reach a position, while `Form conforming?` still reads `yes`, is scoring the block conforming on a rule it never checked; the verdict belongs in `Form conforming?`. `Band` is copied from the chain's own section-4 confidence label, so a disagreement between scan and chain is visible rather than reconciled silently. `Act attempted?` records whether the run tried to open a cited source for that chain's head inputs, and `Edges fired` which bounded re-entry edges fired for it. 91	## Exceptions Summary
92	
93	Three conditions relax the HIGH-confidence requirements introduced into Criteria 3 and 5.
94	This section is a navigation aid, listing them together for quick reference; where its
95	wording differs from the per-criterion clause, the per-criterion clause governs.
96	
97	**(a) Unreachable source** — Criterion 3. A ground truth cites a source the Phase 3
98	verification step could not open; the Phase 3 failure record naming which source and why
99	unreachable is the satisfying evidence; the ground truth may feed only MEDIUM or LOW chains.
100	
101	**(b) Speculative chain** — Criterion 5. A chain is explicitly marked speculative and the
102	analysis states the claim it supports is not load-bearing; the mark plus that statement is
103	the satisfying evidence; the chain may remain MEDIUM. Its confidence line still gives each of
104	its own downgrade causes what would remove it or an explicit account of why no available
105	evidence settles it, because the mark is not a no-path reason. A speculative chain cited on
106	another chain's head is load-bearing and no longer qualifies. A speculative chain with no
107	verification path is therefore not cited on another chain's head; it stays speculative or
108	moves to Abandoned Reasoning.
109	
110	**(c) Absent-fails derivation** — Criterion 5. A chain establishes that a conclusion does not
111	follow from an assumption shown to be false; the named false assumption is the satisfying
112	evidence; the chain may remain MEDIUM.
113	
114	An exception is claimed, not assumed: an analysis relying on one names it in the relevant
115	verdict block and cites the required evidence; an unclaimed exception is not applied on the
116	analysis's behalf.

120	## Scoring Model
121	
122	Score each of the 6 criteria using this shared 4-level scale, applied uniformly across all criteria
123	(highest to lowest):
124	
125	- **Rigorous** — the criterion's named artifact is present, structurally complete, and every
126	  entry meets the observable descriptor for this level: all required fields are populated with
127	  non-generic content, all required relationships are explicit,
128	  and every observable structural test in this criterion's Rigorous descriptor returns pass.
129	
130	- **Sound** — the criterion's named artifact is present and mostly meets the Rigorous descriptor,
131	  but one or more entries fall short in a specific, identifiable way: a field is generic or vague
132	  rather than empty, a relationship is implicit rather than absent, or one entry departs from the
133	  prescribed form without invalidating the rest.
134	
135	- **Hand-wavy** — the criterion's named artifact is present but fails the Rigorous descriptor in
136	  a pattern rather than an isolated entry: multiple fields are generic or empty, the artifact's
137	  prescribed structure is not followed, or the section uses the honest-depth escape valve with a
138	  reason that could be copy-pasted to any analysis without modification.
139	
140	- **Absent** — the criterion's named artifact is missing entirely, or the section exists but
141	  contains no content that could be scored against the artifact's descriptor (the section heading
142	  appears with nothing substantive below it).
143	
144	**Rank order (explicit):** Rigorous > Sound > Hand-wavy > Absent.
145	
146	**Gate:** Any criterion scored **Absent** fails the entire analysis — it must be revised and
147	re-scored, bounded to at most one re-perception pass per analysis, per "How to Apply This
148	Gate" above. If the criterion still scores Absent after that single pass, it is presented as
149	an unresolved gap with a stated confidence caveat instead of being withheld, regardless of how
150	all other criteria score.
151	
152	**Hand-wavy cap:** Two or more criteria scored **Hand-wavy** also fails the entire analysis —
153	the same bound applies: revise and re-score once, per "How to Apply This Gate" above. One
154	criterion at Hand-wavy is tolerated (one isolated weaker section does not indicate a systemic
155	quality problem); two or more at Hand-wavy indicates a pattern of shallow reasoning that the
156	gate alone cannot catch, because no single criterion has reached the gate-fail level. If two or
157	more criteria still score Hand-wavy after that single pass, the cap breach is presented as an
158	unresolved gap with a stated confidence caveat instead of being withheld.
159	
160	**Pass:** No criterion scores Absent, and at most one criterion scores Hand-wavy.
161	(Equivalently: every criterion is Sound or above, except at most one may be Hand-wavy.)
162	
163	**Escape-valve scoring (global rule, applies to every criterion):** Any section that
164	legitimately uses the honest-depth escape valve (`Nothing material here — [reason]`) is
165	scored **Rigorous** if the stated reason is specific to this analysis — it names a property
166	of this problem that makes the section's content unnecessary — and **Hand-wavy** if the
167	reason is generic or copy-pasteable to any analysis. A properly-used escape valve is
168	**never** scored Absent solely for using the escape valve: the per-criterion Absent
169	descriptors below apply to a section that is missing, empty, or filled with non-scoreable
170	content, not to a section that is honestly and specifically marked as having no material
171	content.
172	
173	**Load-bearing chain (definition):** A derivation chain is *load-bearing* if a claim in
174	the Conclusion section (output section 6) depends on it — i.e., the chain produces, or is
175	cited as support for, a conclusion the analysis actually presents. A chain that reaches
176	only an intermediate result no conclusion rests on is not load-bearing. (This is the
177	narrower scoring sense of the phrase `SKILL.md` uses informally as "load-bearing for a
178	high-stakes conclusion.")
179	
180	---
181	
182	## Verdict Block Format
183	
184	The six verdict blocks are emitted together under the single top-level heading
185	`## Self-Audit Gate (process output)`, one `##` heading holding all six in criterion order —
186	the same placement the adversarial pass record and the self-audit scan prescribe for themselves.
187	They are one artifact, not six; nesting them beneath another section's heading makes them a
188	subsection of something they do not belong to, and a reader or a check keyed to that heading
189	must find it in the same structural position on every run.
190	
191	Each of the 6 criteria requires exactly one verdict block. Use the standard form when the
192	analysis section exists and contains scoreable content:
193	
194	```text
195	**Criterion N: [Criterion Name]**
196	Quoted span: "[Direct quote of the specific text that most directly determines the band assigned — from the analysis being scored, or, per the admission below, from the self-audit scan for Criteria 4 and 6 or the Assumption Audit scan for Criterion 2, each emitted as process output for this analysis.]"
197	Band: [**Rigorous** / **Sound** / **Hand-wavy** / **Absent**]
198	Justification: [One sentence tying the quoted span to the observable descriptor for
199	that band — name the specific structural property present or absent.]
200	```
201	
202	The self-audit scan and the Assumption Audit scan are not output sections, and they are the only artifacts outside the six-section analysis a verdict block may quote: the self-audit scan for Criteria 4 and 6, and the Assumption Audit scan for Criterion 2. Every other criterion quotes the analysis text itself, and the §6→§4 closure ledger is admitted nowhere — it is a drafting artifact that describes a document other than the one being scored.
203	
204	Use the gap-citation form when the criterion scores Absent because the section or named
205	artifact is missing or empty — in that case there is no span to quote, and the documented
206	absence is the evidence:
207	
208	```text
209	**Criterion N: [Criterion Name]**
210	Gap: [Name what is missing and where it should have appeared — e.g., "No Derivation
211	Chains section exists; chains of the form 'GT-N + GT-M → [intermediate] → [conclusion]'
212	should appear in section 4 (Derivation Chains) for each conclusion stated in section 6
213	(Conclusion)."]
214	Band: Absent
215	Justification: [One sentence: the absence itself is the structural failure that triggers
216	the gate — the criterion cannot be scored against a non-existent artifact.]
217	```
218	
219	Verdict blocks (not a consolidated table) are required because each block contains a quoted
220	span or a gap citation. Without that span, the evidence-quoting requirement cannot be audited:
221	a summary table of band labels can be produced by asserting compliance, but a verdict block
222	containing a quote that contradicts its claimed band creates a contradiction that cannot be
223	sustained.
224	
225	---
226	
227	## Criteria
228	
229	Apply all six criteria in the order listed. Criteria 1-5 follow the order of the
230	six-section output format — the same chain-of-artifacts sequence the analysis itself
231	follows — so that a scoring pass moves through the analysis in the order it was produced;
232	Criterion 6 is a whole-document cross-section check applied last.
233	
234	### Criterion 1: Identify Essence
235	
236	Scores the **Essence Statement** — the single sentence naming the core problem followed by
237	a short list of success criteria — in the Problem Essence section (output section 1).
238	
239	- **Rigorous** — the Essence Statement is a single sentence that names the core question or
240	  decision (not a symptom, not the triggering event, not a restatement of the user's prompt);
241	  each success criterion contains a pass/fail structural test — a verb + subject + outcome
242	  triplet where the outcome is a property of the Conclusion section — so that a reviewer
243	  applies each criterion by scanning the Conclusion section without analyst interpretation;
244	  the statement is specific enough that it appears nowhere in an analysis of a different but
245	  related problem without modification (it names a property unique to this problem, not a
246	  generic template phrase).
247	  If this section uses the honest-depth escape valve (`Nothing material here — [reason]`), the
248	  stated reason is specific to this analysis's problem — it names a property of the problem
249	  that makes an Essence Statement unnecessary or redundant, and that reason appears in no
250	  other analysis without alteration.
251	
252	- **Sound** — the Essence Statement exists and names a question, but the success criteria are
253	  vague or stated in terms that cannot be verified against the conclusion without further
254	  clarification (e.g., "the solution should be good," "the approach should be appropriate").
255	
256	- **Hand-wavy** — the Essence Statement exists but names a symptom, a triggering event, or a
257	  restatement of the user's prompt rather than the underlying question; OR the success criteria
258	  are absent while the Essence Statement itself is present; OR the section uses the honest-depth
259	  escape valve with a reason that is generic and would apply equally to any analysis (e.g.,
260	  "no essence was needed").
261	
262	- **Absent** — no Essence Statement is present (the Problem Essence section is empty, contains
263	  only a restatement of the original prompt with no analytical distillation, or the section
264	  heading appears with nothing below it).
265	  This verdict routes back to Phase 1 to re-frame the Essence Statement — or, when the cause is an input that was never supplied, to re-opening input under the Input Contract — rather than an in-place rewrite of output section 1; the route is bounded by the same rule described under `SKILL.md`'s "Before presenting conclusions" section.
266	
267	### Criterion 2: Challenge Assumptions
268	
269	Scores the **Classified Assumptions Table** — a table with columns Assumption, Type, Treatment,
270	Verdict, Verification — in the Assumptions Table section (output section 2). Folds in:
271	four-type classification quality and unverified-flag discipline (D-07).
272	
273	- **Rigorous** — every row in the Assumptions Table has a Type value drawn from exactly the
274	  four-type scheme (physical law / current constraint / convention / untested belief); the
275	  Treatment cell uses the vocabulary of the prescribed treatment for that type; the Verdict
276	  cell records Accept, Challenge, or Discard as a leading token followed by an em-dash and a
277	  specific justification — not the bare token alone; the Verification cell cites a specific
